title: Sketch Easel Hinge Solution
content: Blog reader Mel Barranco wanted to build a Sketch Easel, but had limited tools. Despite that limitation, he figured out some clever design solutions that I'd like to share with you.If you've tried to build one, you'll know that one of the design challenges is that theadjustable torque hingesdon't fold all the way flat. His workaround was to replace the protruding adjustment screws with "Chicago Screws" (Thanks, Glenn), normally used for binding papers.He bought the wood from a home improvement store and he didn't have a saw at home, so they cut it for him.He inset the hinges so that they're flush with the work surface, and anchored the hinges withaluminum flat barson the back surfaces. The home improvement store let him use their hacksaw for the aluminum.Thank you, Mel! It's a clever build solution and you canread all about it on his blog. If you would like to shareyourSketch Easel project with the GJ community, please check out my new Facebook Group page, "Sketch Easel Builders."----Previously:Blog post:How to Make a Sketch EaselYour Sketch Easel DesignsYour New Easel BuildsOther resources:"How to Make a Sketch Easel" on GumroadHow to Make a Sketch EaselDVD on Amazon
